title: Particle Physics
subject: Particles & Fields
summary: A survey of the Standard Model following Griffiths: particle zoo and history, relativistic kinematics, symmetries, bound states, the Feynman calculus, QED, QCD, weak interactions and neutrinos, and gauge theories with the Higgs mechanism.

units.title: The Particle Landscape
units.summary: How the electron, photon, antimatter, neutrinos, strange particles and quarks were discovered, what the Standard Model contains, and how forces become Feynman diagrams.

lessons.title: From the electron to antimatter, mesons and neutrinos
objectives: Order the key discoveries (electron, nucleus, photon, positron, neutron, muon, pion, neutrino) and state which puzzle each one solved or created
Explain why beta-decay energy spectra forced Pauli's neutrino hypothesis
Explain Dirac's prediction of the positron and Yukawa's prediction of the pion from the range of the nuclear force
Distinguish leptons, hadrons, mesons and baryons by their interactions

lectures.title: Introduction to Nuclear and Particle Physics: full video-lecture series (11 chapters)
Lecture 0.5: Early History and People in Nuclear and Particle Physics

demoIdeas: Timeline explorer: scroll through 1897-1983 and see the particle table fill in as each discovery lands

lessons.title: Strange particles, the Eightfold Way, quarks and the Standard Model inventory
objectives: State what strangeness is and why strange particles are produced in pairs but decay slowly
List the quarks and leptons with charge and generation structure and the gauge bosons with the force each carries
Build the lowest meson and baryon multiplets from quark content and state the quark charges needed to get integer hadron charges
Cite the evidence for colour and for a fourth and fifth quark (November Revolution, J/psi)

readings.title: The November Revolution and Its Aftermath

demoIdeas: Quark-content builder: drag u, d, s quarks and antiquarks into a hadron and read off charge, strangeness, baryon number and name

lessons.title: Forces, the Yukawa potential and Feynman diagrams as pictures
objectives: Derive the Yukawa potential from the massive-field equation and relate its range to the mediator mass
Read a Feynman diagram as a process: identify external lines, internal lines and vertices, and track conserved charges at each vertex
Compare the strengths and ranges of the four forces and the typical lifetime scale for strong, electromagnetic and weak decays
Use a diagram to enumerate lowest-order contributions to a decay or scattering process
demoIdeas: Yukawa versus Coulomb: overlay potentials for different mediator masses and show the cut-off range

units.title: Relativistic Kinematics
units.summary: Four-vectors and invariants applied to particle decays, collisions, thresholds and collider energies.

lessons.title: Four-vectors, invariants and natural units
objectives: Work in natural units (hbar = c = 1) and convert masses, lengths, lifetimes and cross sections to and from SI/MeV-fm
Apply a Lorentz boost to an energy-momentum four-vector and compute invariant mass squared
Compute energy and momentum of a particle in the lab and centre-of-momentum frames
Use E^2 = p^2 + m^2 to decide whether a process is kinematically allowed
demoIdeas: Boost calculator: enter a four-vector and a boost velocity, see the transformed vector with the invariant mass held constant

lessons.title: Collisions, two-body decays and thresholds
objectives: Compute the final-state momenta in a two-body decay in the parent's rest frame
Compute the invariant s for fixed-target and collider setups and the threshold energy to produce a heavier state
Explain the advantage of colliders over fixed targets in available centre-of-mass energy
Apply the same algebra to a chemical analogue: kinetic-energy release in molecular fragmentation versus nuclear decay
demoIdeas: Threshold tool: pick beam and target particles and see the minimum beam energy for a chosen final state, fixed-target versus collider

units.title: Symmetries, Hadrons and Bound States
units.summary: Conservation laws and symmetry groups, isospin and flavour SU(3), the discrete symmetries C, P, T, and the bound-state spectroscopy of positronium, quarkonium and hadrons.

lessons.title: Symmetries and conservation laws, angular-momentum addition, spin 1/2
objectives: State Noether's theorem informally: each continuous symmetry gives a conserved quantity
Add two angular momenta and state the allowed total J values and the Clebsch-Gordan structure for two spin-1/2 particles
Construct the spin singlet and triplet states and identify their symmetry under exchange
Relate this to chemistry: electron-spin coupling in molecules, NMR J-coupling and term symbols use the same algebra
demoIdeas: Clebsch-Gordan coupler: pick j1, j2 and see the coupled basis and coefficients as a table

lessons.title: Isospin, flavour symmetry and the Eightfold Way
objectives: Explain isospin as an SU(2) symmetry of the strong force and assign I and I3 to the nucleon, pion and delta
Combine two isospins to predict relative rates of strong reactions (e.g. pion-nucleon scattering) with Clebsch-Gordan coefficients
Draw the SU(3) flavour octet and decuplet for the lowest baryons and mesons in the I3-Y plane
Explain why SU(3) flavour is only approximate and relate the mass splittings to the strange-quark mass
demoIdeas: Weight diagram: draw the SU(3) octet and decuplet in I3-Y space and click a state to see its quark content

lessons.title: Discrete symmetries: parity, charge conjugation, CP and time reversal
objectives: Define the parity and charge-conjugation operations and assign intrinsic parity to particles and antiparticles
Compute the parity and C of a quark-antiquark meson with given L and S
State which interactions violate P, C and CP and cite the experimental evidence (Wu experiment, neutral kaons)
State the CPT theorem and explain why it is believed to hold
demoIdeas: Mirror test: a decay-distribution viewer that flips the helicity of the decay products to show parity violation in weak versus conservation in EM decays

lessons.title: Bound states: hydrogen, positronium, quarkonium and hadron spectroscopy
objectives: Scale hydrogen energy levels to positronium and to quarkonium by replacing the reduced mass and the effective coupling
Explain the hyperfine splitting of hydrogen and positronium in terms of spin-spin coupling and extend it to meson and baryon mass splittings
Use the charmonium and bottomonium spectra as evidence for a confining potential with a Coulomb-like short-range part
Compute baryon magnetic moments in the quark model and compare with data
Relate to chemistry: reduced-mass scaling, the 21 cm line and electron-nuclear hyperfine coupling in EPR
demoIdeas: Spectrum scaler: choose hydrogen, positronium, or a heavy-quark potential and compare level diagrams

units.title: The Feynman Calculus
units.summary: Decay rates and cross sections from Fermi's golden rule, and the Feynman rules for a toy theory as a template for the real ones.

lessons.title: Lifetimes, cross sections and the golden rule
objectives: Define decay width, branching ratio, lifetime, cross section and luminosity and relate them
State Fermi's golden rule for decays and scattering with relativistic phase space and the invariant amplitude M
Derive the two-body decay rate formula in the parent rest frame
Relate the width to the energy uncertainty and a resonance line shape (Breit-Wigner), connecting to natural linewidth in spectroscopy
demoIdeas: Breit-Wigner: slide mass and width and see the resonance line shape, with decay time on a parallel panel

lessons.title: Feynman rules for a toy theory and higher-order diagrams
objectives: State the toy-theory Feynman rules (vertex factor, propagator, momentum conservation, integration over loop momenta)
Compute the lowest-order amplitude and decay rate for A -> B + C in the toy theory
Compute the lowest-order scattering amplitude and cross section for two particles exchanging a virtual particle
Explain why higher-order diagrams bring loop integrals that diverge and what renormalisation conceptually does about it

readings.title: Feynman Rules for a Toy Theory

demoIdeas: Diagram builder: attach vertices according to toy-theory rules and see the amplitude expression assembled symbolically

units.title: Quantum Electrodynamics and Chromodynamics
units.summary: The Dirac equation and Feynman rules for QED, standard QED processes, running coupling, and the colour theory of quarks with confinement and asymptotic freedom.

lessons.title: The Dirac equation, antiparticles and the Feynman rules of QED
objectives: Write the Dirac equation and the gamma-matrix algebra, and solve for free-particle spinors of spin up and down
Explain how negative-energy solutions are reinterpreted as antiparticles
State the polarisation vectors of the photon and the QED vertex and propagator factors
Assemble the amplitude for a tree-level QED process (e.g. electron-muon scattering) from the rules

readings.title: The Feynman Rules for Quantum Electrodynamics

demoIdeas: Dirac spinor viewer: plot the four-component spinor for chosen momentum and spin and see the small-component growth with velocity

lessons.title: QED processes, Casimir's trick, cross sections and running coupling
objectives: Use Casimir's trick to convert a spin-averaged squared amplitude into a trace of gamma matrices
Compute the lowest-order cross section for electron-muon scattering or electron-positron annihilation to muon pairs
Explain vacuum polarisation as charge screening and state how alpha runs with energy
Relate the Lamb shift and the anomalous magnetic moment of the electron to loop corrections (spectroscopy connection)

lectures.title: Lecture 4.9: Renormalization and Higher-Order QED Diagrams

demoIdeas: Running coupling: plot alpha(Q) and alpha_s(Q) against energy and mark the Z mass

lessons.title: QCD: colour, confinement and asymptotic freedom
objectives: Explain the role of colour in baryon wave functions (Delta++) and in the ratio R = sigma(hadrons)/sigma(mu mu)
State the Feynman rules of QCD, including the three- and four-gluon vertices, and the colour factor 4/3
Explain how gluon self-interaction produces antiscreening and asymptotic freedom, contrasted with QED screening
Describe deep inelastic scattering and the parton picture, jets at colliders, and confinement/hadronisation
demoIdeas: R-ratio plot: step-function pattern of R versus sqrt(s) across quark thresholds with resonances

units.title: Weak Interactions and Neutrinos
units.summary: Charged-current weak decays, the V-A structure, quark mixing, and neutrino masses and oscillations.

lessons.title: Charged weak decays, V-A structure and quark mixing
objectives: Draw and interpret the lowest-order diagrams for muon decay, neutron beta decay and charged-pion decay
Explain the V-A structure, left-handed projection and helicity suppression of pion decay to electrons relative to muons
Write the CKM matrix, state its role in flavour-changing decays, and explain the origin of CP violation as a complex phase
Estimate decay rates by dimensional analysis using the Fermi constant, including the G_F^2 m^5 scaling
demoIdeas: CKM unitarity triangle: plot the triangle for measured matrix elements and shrink the error bars

lessons.title: Neutrino masses and oscillations
objectives: Explain how a mismatch between flavour and mass eigenstates produces oscillations and derive the two-flavour oscillation probability
Compute oscillation lengths for given energy and mass-squared difference and interpret solar and atmospheric experiments
State the PMNS matrix structure and the evidence for non-zero neutrino masses
Describe the Dirac versus Majorana question and neutrinoless double beta decay

lectures.title: Lecture 8.5: Results of Neutrino Oscillation Experiments

demoIdeas: Oscillation lab: set theta, delta m^2, energy and baseline and watch the flavour probabilities versus L/E

units.title: Gauge Theories, Electroweak Unification and the Higgs
units.summary: Local gauge invariance as the organising principle, electroweak unification, and the Higgs mechanism, at a qualitative-to-semi-quantitative level.

lessons.title: Local gauge invariance and electroweak unification
objectives: Show that requiring local U(1) phase invariance of the Dirac Lagrangian forces a massless photon field to appear
Generalise to non-Abelian gauge theory (Yang-Mills) and say why gauge bosons of SU(2) and SU(3) self-interact
State the field content of electroweak SU(2)xU(1), the weak mixing angle and the relations among W, Z and photon couplings
Explain why explicit mass terms for gauge bosons and chiral fermions break gauge invariance
demoIdeas: Gauge-fix sandbox: apply a position-dependent phase to a wave function and watch the covariant derivative compensate with a gauge field

lessons.title: The Higgs mechanism and the status of the Standard Model
objectives: Explain spontaneous symmetry breaking with the Mexican-hat potential and identify the Goldstone modes
Explain how the Higgs mechanism gives mass to W and Z and to fermions without breaking gauge invariance
State the Higgs production and decay channels used at the LHC and the measured mass and couplings
List the open problems: hierarchy, neutrino masses, dark matter, matter-antimatter asymmetry
demoIdeas: Mexican hat: rotate and tilt the potential to see the vacuum selection and the massive radial versus massless angular modes

exams.title: S1 midterm: landscape, kinematics, symmetries and the Feynman calculus
